before.name: board_renders
before.description:
Open the application and confirm a substantive board renders: a peg board with
two tracks, the ladder, and a control to start a game, without a fatal browser
error or broken page.

before.name: cards_render_as_cards
before.description:
Start a game and confirm the hand renders as recognisable playing cards showing
rank and suit, not as text codes. Confirm the suits are distinguishable and that
hearts and diamonds are red where spades and clubs are not.

after.name: board_renders
after.description:
Open the application and confirm a substantive board renders: a peg board with
two tracks, the ladder, and a control to start a game, without a fatal browser
error or broken page.

after.name: cards_render_as_cards
after.description:
Start a game and confirm the hand renders as recognisable playing cards showing
rank and suit, not as text codes. Confirm the suits are distinguishable and that
hearts and diamonds are red where spades and clubs are not.

before.name: server_backed_local_application
before.description:
Confirm the app is served at localhost:3000 and that its reads and writes use
successful same-origin server requests. A static or local-only mock, a missing
backend, or a non-local game data service does not pass.

before.name: drawn_as_svg_not_images
before.description:
Confirm the cards and the board are drawn as inline SVG rather than fetched
images or a canvas: inspecting a card reveals SVG shapes and text, and no image
file is requested for them.

after.name: server_backed_local_application
after.description:
Confirm the app is served at localhost:3000 and that its reads and writes use
successful same-origin server requests. A static or local-only mock, a missing
backend, or a non-local game data service does not pass.

after.name: drawn_as_svg_not_images
after.description:
Confirm the cards and the board are drawn as inline SVG rather than fetched
images or a canvas: inspecting a card reveals SVG shapes and text, and no image
file is requested for them.

before.name: the_twenty_nine_hand
before.description:
Score the three fives and the jack of clubs with a cut of the five of clubs.
Confirm it totals twenty-nine, the maximum possible hand. Anything else means the
combinations are not all being counted.

before.name: the_app_agrees_with_the_supplied_fixture
before.description:
Take at least eight hands from `club/scored-hands.js`, including the crib ones
and the flush ones, and score each in the app. Confirm every total matches the
file exactly. One disagreement fails this criterion — the file is the bar the
brief sets.

before.name: a_card_counts_in_every_combination
before.description:
Confirm a card is counted in each thing it belongs to rather than once. Score a
hand where one card sits in a fifteen, a pair and a run at the same time, and
check the breakdown credits all three.

before.name: the_crib_flush_needs_five
before.description:
Score four cards of one suit with a cut of a different suit, twice — once as a
hand and once as the crib. Confirm the hand scores four for the flush and the
crib scores none, so the crib total is lower. Treating them the same fails.

before.name: a_five_card_flush_counts_in_both
before.description:
Score the same four cards with a cut of the SAME suit. Confirm the flush now
counts in both the hand and the crib.

before.name: the_ace_is_low_and_does_not_wrap
before.description:
Confirm an ace, two and three with a court card scores a run with the ace low.
Then score jack, queen, king and an ace with a cut of a two, and confirm the run
is THREE — jack, queen, king. A five means the ace has wrapped past the king.

before.name: nobs_needs_the_matching_suit
before.description:
Score a hand holding a jack whose suit matches the cut, and confirm one point for
nobs. Then score the same hand with the jack in a different suit and confirm
there is none.

before.name: fifteen_in_the_play_is_two
before.description:
In the play, lay cards taking the count to exactly fifteen and confirm two points
are given. Confirm the same at thirty-one.

before.name: a_run_in_the_play_need_not_be_in_order
before.description:
Lay a five, then a seven, then a six. Confirm a run of three is scored when the
six lands, rather than nothing.

before.name: the_count_cannot_pass_thirty_one
before.description:
Try to lay a card that would take the count past thirty-one. Confirm it is
refused and the count is unchanged afterwards.

before.name: a_hand_that_is_not_a_hand_is_refused
before.description:
Ask the app to score something invalid — a card that does not exist, a hand of
three cards, or the same card twice. Confirm each is refused with a reason rather
than scored as though it were valid.

before.name: two_cards_each_go_to_the_crib
before.description:
Start a game and confirm each player puts exactly two cards into the crib,
leaving four in hand, and that the crib belongs to the dealer.

before.name: the_crib_is_hidden_until_the_show
before.description:
Confirm neither player can see the other's hand or the crib's contents before the
show. A view that reveals the opponent's cards fails.

before.name: moves_out_of_order_are_refused
before.description:
Try to cut before both players have discarded, and try to discard twice. Confirm
each is refused and the game stays where it was.

before.name: the_show_counts_in_order
before.description:
Reach the show and confirm the counting happens non-dealer first, then dealer,
then the crib, each shown separately with its own total and breakdown.

before.name: the_game_stops_at_the_target
before.description:
Confirm the game ends the moment a player reaches a hundred and twenty-one.

Do NOT try to reach it by playing from nothing: that is thirteen or more hands
and several hundred interactions. Use whatever the app offers for starting a
game near the target — in the reference it is a control for practising the
finish, which begins at 115 to 113 — and play that out instead.

Confirm the winning score is exactly the target and not past it: a board has a
hundred and twenty-one holes, so a hand worth ten counted from a hundred and
fifteen finishes on a hundred and twenty-one. A final score above the target
fails. Confirm the loser is still short, and that the app says the game is over.

If the app offers no way to start near the target, spend no more than a couple
of minutes on this criterion and judge it on what you could observe.

before.name: a_game_is_a_sequence_of_hands
before.description:
Play one hand right through — discard, cut, the play, all three counts of the
show — and confirm the GAME does not end with it. Neither player is near a
hundred and twenty-one after one hand, so the app must offer the next hand and
carry the scores forward, rather than declaring the game over. A game that
finishes after a single hand fails this criterion, and it is the one to check
first: everything about the counting can be right while this is wrong.

before.name: the_deal_alternates_between_hands
before.description:
Across two or more hands, confirm the deal moves from one player to the other
and the app says whose it is. The crib belongs to the dealer, so a deal that
never moves hands the crib to the same player every time. Confirm the hand
count or some equivalent makes it clear which hand is being played.

before.name: a_game_survives_a_reload
before.description:
Part way through a game, reload the page. Confirm the same cards, the crib, the
cut, the peg positions and whose turn it is all come back, rather than a fresh
shuffle.

before.name: the_ladder_updates_when_a_game_ends
before.description:
Note the ladder, finish a game (use the app's near-the-target start rather than
playing from nothing), then confirm the ladder changed: BOTH players' played
count rises by one, and the win goes to the player who actually reached the
target. A win credited to the loser fails, and so does a ladder that never
changes. Reload to confirm it was stored rather than only drawn.

after.name: seed_ladder_import
after.description:
Setup: before any dimension finishes a game, read the supplied records file and open the ladder.
Require all five members with exact stored member numbers, names, played/won counts and all three original game summaries, including unfinished G-1183 with no resumable deal. New games created by other dimensions are allowed; do not require the whole database to contain only seed rows. The visible saved-game chooser must not offer that incomplete historical summary as a playable saved game.

after.name: the_twenty_nine_hand
after.description:
Setup: at the visible hand-scoring bench enter 5S 5H 5D JC, cut 5C, hand mode.
1. Submit through the UI and observe the real local scorer response and rendered result.
2. Require total 29, with fifteens 16, pairs 12, runs 0, flush 0 and nobs 1. A displayed constant without a matching working scorer does not establish this observation.

after.name: the_app_agrees_with_the_supplied_fixture
after.description:
Setup: discover the actual scorer request from a successful visible bench submission. Read all forty supplied records from /assets/club/scored-hands.js.
1. Submit every record with its four cards, cut and hand/crib mode. All forty totals must equal the supplied totals. Preserve a compact table of input, expected and observed result.
2. Inspect representative maximum, zero, overlapping-run and crib-flush records through the visible bench too. Batched requests are permitted only after discovery; they may calculate scores but never create or modify games. Eight examples alone do not satisfy this criterion.

after.name: a_card_counts_in_every_combination
after.description:
Setup: score 4S 5H 5D 6C with cut 9C as a hand through the bench.
Require total 14 with fifteens 6, pairs 2 and runs 6, flush/nobs 0. The duplicated fives participate in both fifteens and both three-card runs as well as their pair; no card is consumed by one scoring category.

after.name: the_crib_flush_needs_five
after.description:
Setup: score 2S 5S 8S KS, cut 9H, through the bench in hand mode and then crib mode.
Require hand total 8, including flush 4 and fifteens 4; crib total 4, with flush 0 and fifteens 4. Preserve each separate result before switching mode.

after.name: a_five_card_flush_counts_in_both
after.description:
Setup: score 2S 5S 8S KS with cut 9S as both a hand and a crib.
Each result must be 9, with flush 5 and fifteens 4. Check both mode submissions; do not infer the crib answer from the hand result.

after.name: the_ace_is_low_and_does_not_wrap
after.description:
Setup: use the scoring bench for these independent hand-mode examples.
1. AS 2H 3D JC, cut KC: total 8, runs 3, fifteens 4 and nobs 1.
2. JS QH KD AC, cut 2C: total 3, runs 3; the ace cannot extend J-Q-K around the top.

after.name: nobs_needs_the_matching_suit
after.description:
Setup: score JS 2H 4D 8C with cut 9S, then change only JS to JH.
Require first total 3 with nobs 1 and fifteens 2, then total 2 with nobs 0 and fifteens 2. Observe each live result.

after.name: fifteen_in_the_play_is_two
after.description:
Setup: use the named Fifteens, runs and thirty-one practice, both starting scores 0; discard each seat's last two listed cards and cut.
1. In a fresh such game play B:5S then A:TH. Require count 15 and exactly +2 to A, with a fifteen explanation.
2. In the separate zero-score P journey defined in the prompt, A:2S takes the count from 29 to 31. Require exactly +2 to A, reset to 0, B leading and no extra go point. These observations must come from actual game moves, not just the scoring bench.

after.name: a_run_in_the_play_need_not_be_in_order
after.description:
Setup: use the zero-score P journey in the prompt.
After B:5S, A:7H, B:6H, require count 18 and exactly +3 to B for the 5-7-6 run, with A still 0. Observe the score and explanation immediately after the third move.

after.name: the_count_cannot_pass_thirty_one
after.description:
Setup: in P play B:5S, A:7H, B:6H, A:TH to reach 28, with B to act and 9D still held.
1. Try B:9D through the visible card control if enabled; require refusal in words. A disabled card with a visible explanation of the count limit is also a valid UI refusal.
2. Using the actual observed play route and shape, submit that same B:9D request directly from the browser. Require a controlled refusal and a fresh unchanged game read, including count 28, hands/laid cards, turn and scores. The valid following B:AC must still work. A toast alone without server nonmutation is insufficient.

after.name: a_hand_that_is_not_a_hand_is_refused
after.description:
Setup: first establish a valid bench result. Use its actual scorer route/shape for malformed cases that the UI cannot express.
Independently submit a non-card ZZ, only three hand cards, a repeated physical card, a null hand-card entry and a missing/invalid cut. Each must return a controlled refusal with a reason, not a total or an unhandled server error. A subsequent valid hand must still score. Submitted fields may follow the app's own schema; test invalid card content rather than golden-only JSON names.

after.name: two_cards_each_go_to_the_crib
after.description:
Setup: start your own zero-score named P practice, dealer A. Before discarding, view each seat through the actual switcher.
1. Each receives the six supplied cards, not a reshuffle.
2. Discard 4S and 6D from A and 8C and KD from B. Each retains exactly its first four supplied cards, crib has four and belongs to A.
3. Cut only after both discards; require the preset QC and B to lead. Capture seat-filtered before/after states through real UI requests.

after.name: the_crib_is_hidden_until_the_show
after.description:
Setup: use your own P game before discards and then after both discards, before cut/play.
1. In each seat view, the other seat's unplayed cards are face down; the response does not contain those card identities, stock or hidden crib contributions in any field. Laid public cards and one's own discards are allowed.
2. After discards, A may know 4S/6D and B may know 8C/KD; neither seat response reveals the other's contribution before it is shown. Inspect both actual seat responses, not merely hidden DOM.
3. Continue that game through the show and require the counted crib to reveal its four cards with its breakdown. This is a deliberate shared seat switcher, not an account-authentication boundary; do not demand passwords or forbid switching seats.

after.name: moves_out_of_order_are_refused
after.description:
Setup: create a fresh P game. Discover action shapes from successful UI requests on your own games.
Try cut before either discard, discard A twice, and a B play while it is A's turn. For each use an observed route/shape, require controlled refusal and fresh unchanged game/ladder state. Establish the invalid precondition first; do not test against a game already moved past it. Keep positive controls: each first valid discard and an in-turn play must work. UI-disabled actions alone do not establish server refusal.

after.name: the_show_counts_in_order
after.description:
Setup: complete zero-score P's eight moves in the prompt; pegging ends with A=3, B=3.
Count through the visible show control. Require separately labelled entries in order non-dealer B (6), dealer A (4), crib A (0), each with its own cards and scoring breakdown. Final scores are A=7, B=9 and phase is between hands. The application may reveal all three ordered entries in one action or step through them. Keep the entries visible until the next hand is requested.

after.name: the_game_stops_at_the_target
after.description:
Setup: start P through the visible practice controls with A=120, B=0, discard and cut normally.
Play B:5S then A:TH. The fifteen awards two but A must stop at exactly 121, B=0, with a named winner/game-over state immediately, no further cards or show. Record game and ladder, then replay the captured winning play and try a later ordinary game action with the observed route/shape. Both refuse without another state/counter change; reload preserves the result. Do not play from zero or rely on a random near-finish deal.

after.name: a_game_is_a_sequence_of_hands
after.description:
Setup: complete zero-score P through all three show entries, using the exact P sequence in the prompt.
1. A=7/B=9 is between hands, not game over; show remains visible until Next hand.
2. Request the next hand once. Preserve the same game identity and scores, increment hand number to 2, deal six cards each and clear only the previous hand's cut, crib, pile, count, laid cards and show. The game continues until a player reaches 121.

after.name: the_deal_alternates_between_hands
after.description:
Setup: use a completed zero-score P hand with dealer A and record its scores.
Next hand makes B dealer, A the next play leader and B owner of the crib; show the hand number and dealer clearly. Play that ordinary hand to its show using legal visible cards, then request the following hand: dealer returns to A and hand number becomes 3. Judge alternation and stable seat ownership independently of the prior criterion's exact P totals.

after.name: a_game_survives_a_reload
after.description:
Setup: create P, complete both discards, cut and play B:5S, A:7H, B:6H. Record game identity, both seat views, crib/own discards, cut QC, laid cards, count 18, scores A=0/B=3, next turn A and hand number 1.
Reload, then use the saved-game chooser in a fresh browser context without the original URL hash/storage to reopen that game. Both seat views must match the saved snapshot, including hidden-card boundaries, and the pegs/turn must agree. Continue with A:TH to prove the saved game is playable, not a static snapshot. Do not require the original browser's chosen seat to transfer to a new device.

after.name: the_ladder_updates_when_a_game_ends
after.description:
Setup: record the two chosen players' actual played/won counts and existing game summaries. Start His heels finish with A=120/B=113, perform both discards and cut JC.
A wins immediately at 121. Both players' played counts increment once; only A's member won count increments once. One finished game summary records the correct members/scores. Replay that captured cut, then reload: no second counter increment or summary. Use relative baselines so prior games do not invalidate the result. Inspect server results as well as the visible ladder.

after.name: hand_order_invariance
after.description:
Setup: discover the scorer through the visible bench. Use hand-mode fixtures 4S 5H 5D 6C/cut 9C (14) and AS AH 2D 2C/cut 3C (16).
Submit all 24 permutations of each four-card hand with unchanged cut. Every result must retain its expected total and breakdown. Batched discovered scoring requests are allowed; record all 48 outcomes. Do not sort or alter the request before sending it to compensate for an app defect.

after.name: pairs_and_last_card_in_real_play
after.description:
Setup: start the Pairs and pair royal practice at 0/0; keep the first four cards per seat and cut QC.
Play B:5S,A:5H,B:5D,A:5C,B:2H,A:2S,B:3H,A:3S.
After the second card A has 2 for a pair; after the third B has 8 (fifteen 2 plus three-of-a-kind 6); after the fourth A has 14 (another 12 for four-of-a-kind). The final card gives A 2 for the pair plus exactly 1 last-card point, ending pegging at A=19/B=8, count 0 and show. Capture each checkpoint before continuing; no duplicate last-card bonus.

after.name: go_resets_and_other_player_leads
after.description:
Setup: start Go and the next lead at 0/0, keep the first four per seat and cut QS.
Play B:TH,A:TS,B:9H. At count 29 neither can lay; require one go point to B, count reset to 0 and A leading, with A=2/B=1. Now A:9S must work. Continue B:8H,A:8S: again neither can lay; A receives pair 2 and go 1, scores A=5/B=1, count 0 and B leading. No manual point claim or illegal over-31 move is needed to trigger go.

after.name: heels_immediate_and_capped
after.description: Setup: use His heels finish. In one game start 0/0, discard the last two per seat and cut JC: A receives exactly 2 immediately before any play; no show entry is added. In a separate game start A=120/B=113 and repeat: A finishes at 121/B=113 immediately, before play or show. Later cut/play/show attempts refuse without changing the finished snapshot. Keep those two games distinct.

after.name: show_wins_stop_at_each_boundary
after.description:
Setup: use three separate Pairs and pair royal practices. In each, discard the last two, cut QC and play B:5S,A:5H,B:5D,A:5C,B:2H,A:2S,B:3H,A:3S. This gives pegging increments A=19/B=8; show totals are non-dealer 10, dealer 10, crib 4.
1. Start A=0/B=104: immediately after non-dealer's count B reaches 121, A remains 19, and no dealer/crib count is awarded.
2. Start A=93/B=0: non-dealer becomes 18; dealer then reaches 121, with no crib count awarded.
3. Start A=89/B=0: dealer is 118 after its hand, then crib reaches exactly 121; B remains 18.
Each result stops at its proper entry and persists after reload; no score exceeds 121. Store checkpoints and judge the three cases independently inside this conjunctive criterion.

after.name: practice_and_scoring_do_not_corrupt_saved_games
after.description:
Setup: create a normal zero-score game and a named fixed practice through the visible controls. Record current games and ladder.
1. Normal game starts at 0/0 with six distinct cards per seat; practice starts accept supplied integer scores from 0 through 120, uses its specified cards/cut and never reshuffles on reload.
2. Negative, fractional and 121-or-higher starting scores are refused without a new game or ladder change. Use the discovered create request if the UI prevents entry.
3. Submit valid hand/pegging bench experiments and invalid/duplicate card experiments. The recorded saved games and ladder remain unchanged. Valid scoring still works after a refusal. Successful game creation may add a saved game, but bench calculations must not.

after.name: pegging_scoring_bench
after.description: Use the visible pegging bench for independent pile/next-card experiments. Require the rendered count, added points and meaningful scoring reasons: [5S]/TH gives count 15 and 2 points; [5S,7H]/6D gives count 18 and run 3; [5S,5H]/5D gives count 15 and 8 points (fifteen 2 plus pair royal 6); [5S,TH,6H,7H,AC]/2S gives count 31 and 2 points. Empty pile with AS gives count 1 and zero points. Over-31 [TS,TH,TD]/2S and duplicate [5C]/5C refuse with a reason, then a valid experiment works again. These are independent hypothetical piles, not permission to modify a real game; saved games and ladder must remain unchanged.

after.name: runtime_manifest_routes
after.description: Read only /app/APP_MANIFEST.md as permitted runtime documentation. Require a fenced bash start command containing node serve.js, the actual SQLite path /app/gambit.db, and main read/scoring/game-action routes consistent with browser-observed requests. GET /api/health must succeed. Verify that the declared database exists and begins with the SQLite file signature; read only its first 16 bytes, without inspecting tables or altering it. Do not inspect implementation source or require golden-only route names for any other endpoint.

after.name: final_restart_persistence
after.description:
Run this last. Record the current full ladder/game summaries, one unfinished playable game's identity and both seat views, and one already finished game's result. Use only the supplied bash /tests/app-lifecycle.sh restart helper to restart the app process, without reseeding or clearing SQLite.
After readiness, reload and reopen the saved game through its chooser; both seat states and ladder summaries must match. The recorded finished game remains finished with unchanged counters. Repeat the process restart once and require the same records with no seed duplication. Continue one legal action on the unfinished game, proving it remains playable. Compare current baselines, not original seed counts.

before.name: theme_or_visual_treatment
before.description:
Confirm the application carries a deliberate visual treatment rather than default
browser styling: a chosen palette applied consistently, considered spacing, and a
type hierarchy in which the card faces, the peg board, the scores and the running commentary are clearly distinguished. If the product
offers a light/dark control, use it and confirm it produces a clear rendered
change while preserving legibility and the current screen. Unstyled controls on a
white page fails.

before.name: responsive_layout
before.description:
At roughly a 390 by 844 mobile viewport, confirm the main content fits without
horizontal page overflow and that the board, the hand, the play area and the ladder remain reachable and usable.

before.name: accessible_controls
before.description:
On the desktop experience, confirm a navigation landmark where the product has
navigation, a main landmark, meaningful headings, and accessible names or
associated labels for the visible buttons, inputs and selects actually used to
operate the game — starting one, choosing cards, cutting and counting.

before.name: interaction_feedback
before.description:
Confirm interactive controls have clear hover or focus feedback. Confirm that
a card that cannot be laid without passing thirty-one is communicated with a visible reason in words rather than by colouring
a control red or failing silently.

before.name: empty_and_transitional_states
before.description:
Open the app before a game has been started and look at the empty board.
 Confirm the state reads as deliberate rather than as a failure or a blank
screen, and that opening and closing any dialog, drawer or panel the product
provides leaves the surrounding screen usable rather than permanently obscured.

after.name: keyboard_controls_and_focus
after.description:
Setup: use the visible game controls, seat switcher and scoring bench with the keyboard.
Require labels/accessible names for starting, choosing cards, discarding, cutting and counting. Tab/Shift+Tab show visible focus; Enter/Space operate cards and buttons; focus after a card action remains on a useful reachable control. No keyboard trap or unintended game mutation from moving focus. Inspect landmarks/headings where applicable; do not demand a navigation landmark when the app has no navigation.

after.name: responsive_controls_and_reachability
after.description: Inspect at 1280 by 800 and 375 by 760. Through normal vertical scrolling, reach the board, active hand, crib/play controls, saved-game chooser, bench and ladder. No horizontal page overflow, clipped essential label or inaccessible action. Card controls and touch targets remain practical. Grade reachability/operability, not decorative composition.

after.name: illegal_move_feedback
after.description:
Setup: start P at zero and play B:5S,A:7H,B:6H,A:TH to reach 28 with B to act. Try B:9D or inspect its disabled-state explanation.
Require a visible textual reason for the over-31 refusal, readable/announced feedback and a still-usable table. Valid B:AC afterward must work. Feedback must not depend solely on red colour or a silent disabled button. Observe actual UI outcomes; exact response codes are not prescribed.

after.name: pending_action_and_empty_state
after.description:
Setup: open the root without selecting a saved game, then start your own zero-score game.
The no-game view explains how to begin. During a real pending game save, rapid repeated activation of that same control must not create duplicate accepted actions/games; show a busy/pending state or suppress repeated activation. Browser network delay may hold one observed request pending, but do not alter its payload or fabricate success. Resume/close controls and any supplied panels leave the surrounding table usable. Do not require dialogs the app does not have.

after.name: readable_state_and_reduced_motion
after.description:
Setup: inspect an active zero-score P game, its show and scoring bench, then emulate reduced motion.
Names, active seat, dealer, turn, hand number, cut, count, scores and scoring commentary are available as text alongside the SVG. Bench totals and separate scoring categories remain readable and clearly separate from ranked game points. Show entries remain readable until Next hand. Nonessential motion is reduced or already absent; no information is lost. Grade semantic clarity and motion support, not visual taste or rechecking score arithmetic.

before.name: visual_typography
before.description:
Assess rendered table, game, scoring bench, ladder and show typography at desktop size.
5: deliberate, readable type sizes and weights distinguish product title,
seat, turn/result, totals and secondary history; alignment is consistent.
4: readable with one or two minor sizing or alignment imperfections.
3: noticeable inconsistent sizing, crowding or awkward text truncation.
2: several important labels or history entries are difficult to read.
1: broadly illegible, misaligned or undifferentiated text.
0: no coherent typographic rendering on the reviewed surfaces.
Do not grade move correctness or exact seed values here.

before.name: visual_color_and_contrast
before.description:
Assess the supplied theme; a theme switcher is not required.
5: cohesive palette with clearly distinguishable red/black suits and both peg tracks, face-down
cards, legible text and purposeful accents across game, scoring bench and show.
4: one or two minor contrast or palette imperfections.
3: some low-contrast text or conflicting accents distract from the board.
2: substantial legibility or piece-distinction problems.
1: widespread low contrast or harsh, incoherent color treatment.
0: no readable color treatment renders.
Judge appearance, not actual winner detection or accessible-name behavior.

before.name: visual_spacing_and_layout
before.description:
Assess spacing on desktop table, peg board, cards, scoring bench, ladder and show.
5: consistent margins and alignment, deliberate board/control grouping and
balanced spacing between totals, history and show.
4: minor uneven spacing or alignment.
3: several crowded, drifting or excessively separated elements.
2: frequent collisions, clipping or inconsistent gutters.
1: broadly unbalanced or broken layout.
0: no coherent spaced layout renders.
Do not require a specific arrangement or the reference's pixels.

before.name: visual_hierarchy_and_scanability
before.description:
Assess how easily the board, turn/result, seat, scores, commentary and scoring breakdown can be
visually located on desktop without reading all surrounding text.
5: clear visual order with primary game state prominent and related secondary
information grouped; the scoring bench is clearly distinct from the active game.
4: mostly clear with minor competing emphasis.
